scope: Mathematical Cayley C4 criterion and abelian corollary only; encoding/group tables/solver controls require separate checks
argument: For h != e, a common neighbor a of e,h corresponds uniquely to (a,a^-1 h) in S x S with product h.
Cancellation makes distinct ordered factorizations have distinct first entries. Since S excludes e, e,a,h,c are four distinct vertices. Inverse closure supplies both undirected closing edges.
Left multiplication by x^-1 is a graph automorphism, so checking all pairs e,h checks all vertex pairs. A simple graph is C4-free exactly when distinct vertices have at most one common neighbor.
For abelian G and |S|>=3, fix a and choose b outside {a,a^-1}; then ab=ba != e yields distinct ordered factorizations.
Repeated representation indicators must remain in AMO: in an abelian group the ordered pairs (a,b) and (b,a) are distinct even if their Boolean conjunctions coincide.
